30 In a uniform electric field, which statement is correct?
A
All charged particles experience the same force.
B
All charged particles move with the same velocity.
C
All electric field lines are directed towards positive charges.
D
All electric field lines are parallel.

hints: Focus on the word uniform - it means electric field strength $E$ has the same magnitude and the same direction at every point in the region.
Connect this to $F = qE$ for a charged particle and to what field-line direction and spacing represent for $E$.
Compare each statement about same force, same velocity, lines towards positive charges, and parallel lines against those two ideas.
walkthrough: Identify the definition: uniform electric field means the field-strength vector $E$ is constant - same magnitude in $\text{N C}^{-1}$ and same direction at all points.

Use $F = qE$ for the force on a particle. Because $F$ is proportional to the particle charge $q$, different charges give different forces, and negative charges feel a force opposite to $E$. So not all particles share the same force or the same motion.
Recall the field-line convention: lines show the direction of the force on a positive test charge, so they leave positive charges and enter negative charges, not towards positive charges.
For constant $E$, the lines must keep the same direction everywhere and the same spacing everywhere, which means straight parallel equally spaced lines. This is option D.

A.explanation: Force is $F = qE$, so particles with different charge $q$ experience different magnitude and possibly different direction of force.

B.explanation: Different charge and mass give different acceleration from $a = qE/m$, so velocities after the same time are not the same.

C.explanation: Field lines are directed away from positive charges and towards negative charges by convention.

D.explanation: A uniform field has the same $E$ magnitude and direction everywhere, shown by parallel equally spaced field lines.
